items.title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
items.abstract: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.

items.title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
items.abstract: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.

items.title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT
items.authors: Jackson R. Fliss, Alan Rios Fukelman, Stathis Vitouladitis
items.abstract: We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the na\"ive cutting map based solely upon path integration subject to boundary conditions is not isometric for generic TQFTs. For any 2d TQFT, we give a prescription to construct isometric cutting maps by dressing path integration with suitable edge operators. This allows us to compute entanglement for any state, any bipartition, and any boundary condition. As a consequence, we find a non-integer "ground-state degeneracy" \`a la Affleck-Ludwig, despite all boundary conditions being gapped. We further show how to reconstruct the partition function of the TQFT at arbitrary genus from the multi-interval R\'enyi entropies of a single state. For theories with (possibly non-invertible) symmetries, we show that the entanglement entropy of the symmetric ground state can distinguish gapped phases with the same symmetry, without any further knowledge of their vacua, while the entanglement asymmetry of the vacua entropically detects symmetry breaking. We illustrate our formalism with a range of applications, from finite gauge theories to Haagerup gapped phases and infrared phases of adjoint QCD$_2$.

items.title: Type IIB instanton corrections from pure modular unfolding
items.abstract: We study the reconstruction of instanton corrections to type IIB higher-derivative interactions from their low Fourier modes using modular symmetry, without invoking supersymmetry differential equations. This provides a framework for studying non-BPS interactions through their modular coefficient functions. For the $D^6R^4$ coefficient, Rankin-Selberg unfolding determines the continuous spectral overlap from the complete zero mode. Assuming the conjectured simplicity of the even cusp spectrum, we extract the cusp amplitudes from Mellin residues of the complete first mode. We combine both contributions to reconstruct all higher Fourier modes, using Hecke relations for the cusp contribution. Using the Kuznetsov trace formula and bounds on the spectral tail, we derive the $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms in the weak-coupling instanton prefactor at every fixed positive charge. The leading term arises collectively from the infinite cusp sum, and both coefficients agree with the known expansion. With incomplete low-mode data, we construct modular ambiguities and give sufficient conditions for the stability of leading higher-charge coefficients. Applied to the supplied $D^8R^4$ data, these results identify the additional information needed for higher-charge predictions.

items.title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading
items.abstract: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.

items.title: Moduli spaces in CFT: vortex defects
items.abstract: We construct and study a class of codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneously broken conformal symmetry, assuming that a continuous global symmetry is also broken on the moduli space. Our construction can be viewed as an analytic continuation of the saddle point describing large charge operators and generalizes known BPS defects in supersymmetric theories, such as Gukov-Witten surface operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and vortex loops in ABJM theory, but does not rely on supersymmetry. These defects are characterized by continuous, unbounded parameters controlling the expectation values of operators parametrizing the moduli space, and interpolate between a quantum regime and a semiclassical regime in which the local physics approaches that of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. This connection allows us to derive exact results from the effective description of the broken phase. In particular, our results for Gukov-Witten surface operators agree with localization, and we compute the $g$-function for a broad class of $1/2$-BPS vortex loops in ABJM theory. Finally, we relate the spectrum of defect operators, in a suitable scaling limit, to the spectrum of massive particles in the symmetry-breaking vacuum.

items.title: Categorical RMT
items.authors: Chuanxin Cui, Kristan Jensen, Sridip Pal, Moshe Rozali
items.abstract: Random matrix theory (RMT) describes the level statistics of chaotic systems one symmetry sector at a time. We propose its analogue for local quantum systems on a circle with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries. Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. Under our proposal, the symmetry fixes exact degeneracies and identifications among sectors, and ordinary RMT describes the rest, with unrelated blocks treated as statistically independent. We call this categorical RMT. For a non-invertible symmetry it goes beyond ordinary RMT, since Hilbert spaces with different twists can share a sector, and so part of their spectrum, though no invertible symmetry relates them. We confirm this in a chaotic Fibonacci anyon chain, and check the framework in chaotic $S_3$ chains. We extend categorical RMT to primary states at fixed spin in 1+1-dimensional CFTs, where modular covariance requires additional correlations. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory. In holographic CFTs, torus wormholes decorated by the SymTFT or by Chern--Simons theory realize the predicted ramp and its modular completion.

items.title: BPS Bootstrap
items.abstract: We apply the large $N$ matrix bootstrap technique to constrain expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states that are dual to classical geometries. For states dual to horizonless geometries, their explicit moduli give rise to large allowable regions in the bootstrap, while for black holes, a converging bootstrap should find islands. We explore this method in $\mathcal{N}=4$ $SU(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory at large $N$, working at weak coupling and focusing on BPS states with scaling dimensions of order $N^2$. For the $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/8$-BPS sectors, the bootstrap finds large regions, in agreement with an eigenvalue description of such states in the limit of large charges. We also present preliminary results for a BMN truncation of the $1/16$-BPS sector, which contains states dual to both horizonless geometries and black holes. Isolating the black hole states in the bootstrap remains a challenge.

items.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
items.authors: Alessio Caddeo, Oscar Henriksson, Carlos Hoyos, Mikel Sanchez-Garitaonandia, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez
items.abstract: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

items.title: Resummations In Higher-Curvature Modifications Of Starobinsky Inflation
items.abstract: We study higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which are expected to be generated at the quantum level. When treated perturbatively in the couplings $\gamma$ of the higher-dimensional operators, these terms produce inverse powers of the slow-roll parameter $\alpha$, casting doubt on the reliability of the slow-roll expansion. If instead $\gamma$ is kept exact, the expansion fails to reproduce the Starobinsky model smoothly as $\gamma\to 0$. We show that this problem is solved by resumming certain series in the ratio $\alpha/\gamma$. The resulting ``improved'' slow-roll expansion is regular in the limit $\gamma\to 0$ and gives the same result whether one expands first in $\gamma$ or in $\alpha$. We illustrate this explicitly for an $R^3$ term, obtain the power spectra, spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio at next-to-leading order in the improved expansion, and show that results in the recent literature are recovered as the first-order Taylor expansion of ours. Comparing with the latest ACT, Planck and SPT data, we find that the resummed and first-order results differ appreciably only for values of $n_s$ outside the favored regions. Finally, we comment on the origin of higher-curvature operators in UV-complete theories, such as renormalizable quantum gravity, where the predictions of the Starobinsky model are stable.

items.title: Rotational instability and quadrupolar order in BFSS matrix theory
items.abstract: We study the effect of angular momentum on thermal states of the BFSS matrix theory in its gravitational and high-temperature classical regimes. We focus on ensembles with only one non-zero angular momentum. On the gravity side, the rotating ensemble is described by the singly-spinning D$0$ black hole. Beyond a critical rotation, we find that this solution becomes unstable to a non-axisymmetric quadrupolar perturbation. Following this mode non-linearly, we find a new branch of non-axisymmetric rotating black holes that is thermodynamically favoured over the axisymmetric branch in both the microcanonical and canonical ensembles. On the other hand, in the classical matrix limit, we find no evidence for such collective quadrupolar order over the matrix sizes and angular momenta studied. Instead, rotation accelerates the separation of a single D$0$-brane from the clump of branes initially prepared. The separated brane carries a large fraction of the angular momentum by orbiting the rest of the clump at a large in-plane radius. Both the angular momentum share and the orbital radius relative to the clump size increase with the matrix size. These results distinguish a collective quadrupolar deformation in the gravity limit from angular-momentum transfer to a single brane in the classical matrix limit.

items.title: Scale separation and partial supersymmetry breaking
items.authors: Niccol\`o Cribiori, Fotis Farakos, Alexandros Zarafonitis
items.abstract: We propose new candidate string theory vacua in which partial supersymmetry breaking occurs within the lower-dimensional effective theory in anti-de Sitter space, parametrically below the Kaluza--Klein scale. These vacua solve the equations of motion of massless type IIA supergravity in the smeared approximation and exhibit parametric scale separation, at both weak and strong string coupling. They are reproduced as $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric phases of a three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ gauged supergravity. Should these vacua be solutions of string theory, they would provide explicit setups in which partial supersymmetry breaking can be studied at energies parametrically below the compactification scale. In addition, we further comment on our previously proposed solution with scale separation and extended supersymmetry.

items.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
items.abstract: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

items.title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
items.authors: Christoph Adam, Andr\'es R. Anad\'on, Carlos Naya, Thomas Winyard
items.abstract: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.

items.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
items.abstract: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/\omega$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

items.title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
items.authors: Qi Chen, Zhongjie Huang, Yunfeng Jiang, Xinan Zhou
items.abstract: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.

items.title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
items.abstract: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.

items.title: Bions and infrared renormalons in K\"ahler sigma models with $U(1)$ isotropy
items.abstract: We study semiclassical bion contributions to the vacuum energy of K\"ahler sigma models with two-dimensional target spaces on $\mathbb{R} \times S^1$ with twisted boundary conditions. This is first illustrated in the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model, where explicit real and complex bion solutions are constructed in a manner analogous to that used in its quantum-mechanical reduction [1]. Evaluating the bosonic and fermionic fluctuations at one loop, we obtain the effective action with both the coupling constant and the elongation parameter properly renormalized. Integration over the bion quasi-moduli space using Lefschetz thimbles then gives the leading nonperturbative contribution, which the real and complex bion contributions cancel at the supersymmetric point, while the first imaginary ambiguity appears when deviating from the supersymmetric point. Requiring its cancellation against the perturbative ambiguity allows us to infer the corresponding infrared-renormalon pole. This is an explicit example generalizing the resurgent structure of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ model in [2] from one coupling to two renormalized parameters. The calculation further extends to K\"ahler targets of one complex dimension with a $U(1)$ symmetry. At leading dilute one-loop order, the target dependence enters through the moment-map difference and the metric normalizations at the two fixed points. The ambiguity structure and infrared scaling of the bion weight are common to these targets, while the inferred pole position depends on the target metric.

items.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlev\'e II
items.authors: Sibasish Banerjee, Babak Haghighat, Jie Sun
items.abstract: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlev\'e II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlev\'e II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.

items.title: Geometry of Gauge-invariant Quantum Fields
items.abstract: Gauge-invariant representatives of massless gauge fields generally involve inverse differential operators. We trace this non-locality to the homotopy contracting the free gauge complex and replace it, at field level, by a local map using an independent scalar and a differential constraint. We discuss the BRST completion needed to preserve the physical content and the relation to the St\"uckelberg theory. We finally comment on the extension of this approach to non-Abelian gauge groups via the extension to interactions through $L_\infty$ homotopy transfer.

items.title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
items.abstract: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.

items.title: Tunneling from an oscillating state in quantum field theory
items.authors: Oliver Janssen, Matthew Kleban, Mehrdad Mirbabayi, Cameron Norton
items.abstract: How does a scalar field oscillating about a metastable minimum decay? For a coherent state with $\langle q(t) \rangle = a \cos mt$ we find two results. When $mR \ll 1$, with $m$ the mass and $R$ the bubble radius, the decay at time $t$ is a Coleman bubble in the frozen potential $U_t(\eta) = U(\langle q \rangle +\eta)-U(\langle q \rangle)-U'(\langle q \rangle)\eta$, for any amplitude. At small amplitude but any $mR$, $B(t)=B_0 - a \mathcal{M} \cos mt+O(a^2)$, with $\mathcal{M}$ set by the tail of the vacuum bounce; for a thin wall $\mathcal{M} \propto e^{mR}$, so exponentially small oscillations change the rate significantly. Both results follow from a Euclidean source construction. The same method computes the tunneling rate of a field slowly rolling in one direction and metastable in another.

items.title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
items.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

items.title: Generalizations of Courant brackets in the T-dual description of a weakly curved string background
items.abstract: When T-duality is realized as a canonical transformation, the standard Courant bracket is T-dual invariant, while the $B$- and $\theta$-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged. We determine how these relations are modified for a closed bosonic string moving in a weakly curved background with a constant metric and a Kalb-Ramond field with linear coordinate dependence. We work to first order in its constant field strength. The T-dual background fields depend on a line integral of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields, making the dual description nonlocal. We construct generalized charges whose parameters depend on this line integral and calculate their Poisson bracket algebra using the T-duality transformation laws and the canonical brackets of the initial theory. The resulting algebra yields a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid. We establish an explicit isomorphism with the standard Courant algebroid by transporting the bracket, pairing, and anchor. Applying $B$- and $\theta$-shifts to the dual currents, we obtain weakly curved generalizations of the respective twisted Courant brackets. We show that these brackets provide the T-dual realizations of the initial $\theta$- and $B$-twisted Courant brackets, respectively, and identify the corresponding Courant algebroid isomorphisms.

items.title: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
items.authors: Konrad Kockler, Jan M. Pawlowski, Vladimir V. Skokov
items.abstract: We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $\eta=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $\epsilon$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $\sigma=0.076$ and $\nu_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_\sigma=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_\sigma$, we obtain $\eta=-0.795(21)$ and $\omega=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$. For the complex Yang-Lee fixed point, convergence of the field expansion depends crucially on its reference point. Expansions about $\phi=0$ fail to converge with the smooth regulator used here, whereas expansions about the running imaginary field value at which the mass vanishes converge down to $d=1.3$. This representation preserves the exact relation between the thermal eigenvalue and the field dimension, and hence the hyperscaling identity $\theta_h+\theta_t=d$, at every field-truncation order. We trace the large violations reported in earlier works to the omission of the expansion-point motion when linearizing the flow, rather than to the truncation itself.

items.title: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
items.abstract: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gr\"obner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.

items.title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
items.abstract: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(\phi^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.

items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
items.abstract: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using L\"uscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI. Finally, we identify metastable resonances in the spectrum.
